title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 7 — WORLD 4: C1 FLUENCY & DISCOURSE MASTERY
description: A C1 fluency world focused on sustained communication, discourse control, sophisticated interaction, and the ability to adapt language naturally across complex academic, social, and professional situations.

targets.vocabulary: 3300+ active words with advanced collocations, idioms, phrasal verbs, and register-sensitive vocabulary
targets.reading: 1900–2300 words with synthesis, rhetorical analysis, inference, and author-position analysis
targets.listening: 20–24 minutes of authentic dialogue, interviews, presentations, and spontaneous discussion
targets.speaking: 24–30 minutes of sustained interaction, argumentation, explanation, and spontaneous follow-up
targets.writing: 650–850 words with sophisticated organization, synthesis, nuance, and audience awareness
targets.presentation: 12–15 minute presentation with structured interaction and unscripted Q&A

grammar: Advanced tense and aspect for narrative viewpoint and discourse management
Modal and semi-modal systems for subtle certainty, obligation, criticism, and inference
Participle clauses and reduced structures for concise formal expression
Inversion and fronting for emphasis and rhetorical effect
Advanced relative clauses and noun phrase modification
Concession, qualification, contrast, and logical sequencing
Hedging, boosters, stance, politeness, and interpersonal meaning

missions.title: Fluency Engine
missions.focus: automatic retrieval, collocations, chunks, and flexible sentence patterns
missions.challenge: Maintain natural flow while selecting precise language under time pressure.

missions.title: Discourse Architecture
missions.focus: topic development, paragraph logic, signposting, and discourse structure
missions.challenge: Build a long response that remains coherent from opening idea to final conclusion.

missions.title: Advanced Paraphrase Lab
missions.focus: reformulation, compression, expansion, and semantic equivalence
missions.challenge: Express the same complex meaning in several natural and context-appropriate ways.

missions.title: Rhetorical Precision
missions.focus: emphasis, contrast, inversion, fronting, and persuasive sentence design
missions.challenge: Use advanced structures to make important information stand out without sounding forced.

missions.title: Stance & Position Lab
missions.focus: certainty, probability, evaluation, criticism, and author stance
missions.challenge: Communicate a position while controlling exactly how strongly each claim is presented.

missions.title: Argument Connector
missions.focus: concession, counterargument, qualification, and logical progression
missions.challenge: Connect competing ideas into a balanced and convincing line of reasoning.

missions.title: Conversation Navigation
missions.focus: turn-taking, interruption, clarification, repair, and topic management
missions.challenge: Enter, redirect, sustain, and close complex conversations naturally.

missions.title: Diplomatic English Arena
missions.focus: indirect disagreement, tact, mitigation, and relationship-sensitive language
missions.challenge: Handle disagreement without losing clarity, professionalism, or rapport.

missions.title: Humor, Irony & Implication
missions.focus: implied meaning, irony, understatement, exaggeration, and contextual interpretation
missions.challenge: Recognize and respond appropriately when speakers communicate beyond literal wording.

missions.title: Advanced Discussion Arena
missions.focus: extended discussion, spontaneous questions, challenge-response, and synthesis
missions.challenge: Sustain a demanding discussion while responding directly to unexpected ideas.

missions.title: Rhetorical Reading Lab
missions.focus: argument structure, tone, rhetorical choices, assumptions, and evidence
missions.challenge: Explain not only what a text says, but how its language shapes interpretation.

missions.title: Listening Under Pressure
missions.focus: fast speech, overlapping ideas, reformulation, hesitation, and speaker intent
missions.challenge: Follow authentic speech even when speakers change direction or qualify themselves.

missions.title: Synthesis Writing Lab
missions.focus: combining multiple sources, comparison, evaluation, and integrated argument
missions.challenge: Synthesize information from different perspectives into one coherent written response.

missions.title: Executive Communication
missions.focus: briefings, summaries, recommendations, and decision-focused writing
missions.challenge: Turn complex information into concise communication for a busy professional audience.

missions.title: Presentation Command
missions.focus: opening, narrative structure, transitions, emphasis, visuals, and Q&A
missions.challenge: Lead an extended presentation while adapting explanations to audience reactions.

missions.title: Conflict Resolution Simulation
missions.focus: clarification, reframing, compromise, persuasion, and mediation
missions.challenge: Resolve a realistic disagreement through precise and relationship-aware communication.

missions.title: Global Communication Lab
missions.focus: intercultural communication, global English, register, and audience adaptation
missions.challenge: Adjust language and interaction style for people with different linguistic and cultural backgrounds.

missions.title: Academic & Professional Roundtable
missions.focus: seminar discussion, workplace strategy, evidence, questions, and collaboration
missions.challenge: Contribute substantial ideas while accurately building on, challenging, and clarifying others' points.

missions.title: World 4 Integrated Fluency Marathon
missions.focus: integrated C1 reading, listening, speaking, writing, grammar, and vocabulary
missions.challenge: Complete a multi-stage communication sequence with minimal preparation and limited support.

missions.title: WORLD 4 MASTER QUEST — C1 FLUENCY & DISCOURSE
missions.focus: full-world mastery assessment
missions.challenge: Demonstrate sustained, coherent, precise, flexible, and socially appropriate C1 communication across complex tasks.

realWorldScenarios: Leading a meeting where several participants disagree about priorities
Explaining a complicated issue to a non-specialist audience
Comparing two proposals and recommending a course of action
Participating in a seminar discussion with spontaneous follow-up questions
Writing an executive summary from multiple information sources
Mediating a conflict while maintaining trust and professional relationships

assessment.format: Integrated C1 fluency and discourse assessment
assessment.masteryGoal: Learner can sustain sophisticated communication, organize complex discourse, adapt register, and express nuanced meaning naturally and independently at C1 level.
